draft.title: Price and perceived quality
card: Perceived quality is how good customers believe a product is. It is a belief, not a measured fact.
When customers cannot easily judge quality for themselves, they often use price as a clue. A high price can suggest a better product.
This is most likely with premium brands, such as luxury watches or designer clothing, where image is part of what the customer buys.
Cutting the price of a premium brand can lower its perceived quality and damage its image. Sales may rise for a time, but loyal customers may leave.
draft.remember: A price sends a message about quality, so a cut can weaken a premium brand.

a.q: Why might a large price cut harm a premium handbag brand?
opts: Customers may read the lower price as lower quality
Customers always stop buying when a price falls
Customers cannot tell that the price has changed
Customers expect every brand to have a similar price
a.why: Customers often use price as a clue to quality, so a deep cut can make the brand look less special. The cut does not always stop buying, since some customers may buy more, but the damage to image is the risk.
a.clue: Think about what a high price tells a buyer.

b.q: Kiri owns a Hobart skincare brand sold as a luxury product. Sales are slow, so she is thinking of halving the price. What is the main risk of this?
opts: The brand may look lower in quality to customers
The product will cost more to make than before
Customers will not notice any change in the price
Competitors will be unable to change their prices
b.why: Her brand relies on a luxury image, and a high price helps signal quality. Halving the price may lead customers to see it as ordinary. The cost of making the product does not change because the selling price changes.
b.clue: What does the luxury image depend on?

a.best: Customers may read the lower price as lower quality

b.best: The brand may look lower in quality to customers

proposal.title: Price and perceived quality
card: Perceived quality is how good customers believe a product is. It is a belief, not a measured fact, so it can change even when the product does not.
When customers cannot easily judge quality for themselves, they often use price as a clue. A high price can suggest a better product.
This is most likely with premium brands, such as luxury watches or designer clothing, where image is part of what the customer buys.
Cutting the price of a premium brand can lower its perceived quality and damage its image. Sales may rise for a time, but loyal customers may leave.
proposal.remember: A price sends a message about quality, so a cut can weaken a premium brand.

a.q: Why might a large price cut harm a premium handbag brand?
opts: Buyers link the lower price with lower quality
Buyers judge quality only by measured facts
Buyers stop buying any product whose price falls
Buyers think every handbag brand should cost the same
a.why: Customers often use price as a clue to quality, so a deep cut can make the brand look less special. A price cut does not stop all buying, since sales may rise for a time, but the damage to image is the risk.
a.clue: Think about what a high price tells a buyer.

b.q: Kiri owns a Hobart skincare brand sold as a luxury product. Sales are slow, so she is thinking of halving the price. What is the main risk of this?
opts: Customers come to see the brand as lower in quality
Customers notice the product itself has been changed
Customers stop using price as a clue to quality
Customers see the brand as better value than before
b.why: Her brand relies on a luxury image, and a high price helps signal quality. Halving the price can make customers see it as ordinary, even though the product is the same. Seeing it as better value is a possible benefit, not the main risk to a luxury brand.
b.clue: What does the luxury image depend on?

a.best: Buyers link the lower price with lower quality

b.best: Customers come to see the brand as lower in quality
